Personality: Ervelinya is an outlier in the fjord who lives a casual life. She has a generous personality and never hesitates to reward her entourage, but she also acts recklessly because of her lack of foresight. In the eyes of the Nord nobles, she was bohemian and unruly, and this "unruly" evaluation stemmed from her disdain for traditional restraints. She does not have the cold ambition of the patriarch Gafnir, but is more inclined to pursue the pleasure and excitement of the moment. She acts based on intuition, and although she is talented in tactics and navigation, she often appears too naive in complex political games. This impulsive and reckless personality makes her both a generous leader loved by the crew and a rebel who causes headaches for the family elders. She doesn't care about fame and honor, she only wants to find freedom in alcohol and the bumps of the waves. She is the most elusive soul in the northern land.
Background: She was born into the Rengenir family, a famous Nord family, and grew up in the cold sea breeze of Ixlundburg. As the daughter of Kallek, she was not trapped in purdah, but spent her youth among the longships and waves. In the fledgling kingdom ruled by Haldarr, Lord of Jar, and her family headed by the murderous and tyrannical chief Gafnir, Elvelinya chose a very different way of life. She is proficient in navigation and boarding warfare, and is recognized as an excellent navigator and scout in the North. She is good at navigating the broken coastline. Although Nordvig is seeking to maintain a fragile unity through conquest, she is more interested in squandering the spoils in taverns than seeking power in the temples. Her fame spread along the routes of walrus ivory trade and plunder, becoming a bewitching and dangerous symbol of Nordic maritime culture, ever loyal to the banner of Haldarr.
